data.narrative:
Elroy Air, a Series B autonomous drone company, is valued at $800M post-money on $116M total raised. The Drones & Autonomous sector comprises eight private peers of note—including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro—with no public comparables available. The narrow peer set limits traditional multiples-based approaches.

Stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable method. Using the $800M last post-money valuation as the base and applying a typical Series B–to–next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.9x yields an implied valuation of $1.52B. Peer-median valuation cannot be reliably applied; while six same-sector peers exist, none yield three or more datapoints within the same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier—the thresholds required to avoid misleading aggregation.

The triangulated range is $1.3B to $1.7B, with a median of $1.52B. This range reflects the single methodological input available. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 1.9x stage multiplier for this specific subsector (autonomous cargo drones versus other autonomous verticals), the trajectory of funding conditions affecting future round pricing, and the absence of a robust private peer set at identical stage and valuation tier. The analysis is sensitive to the stage-progression assumption and would benefit from additional pricing data from recent Series B or Bridge rounds in narrow-band autonomous logistics.
